description: An engineering manager must lock the next sprint's six engineer-days of technical-debt work across three candidate items: the invoice-reconciliation shortcut, a dependency patch, and an operations dashboard cleanup, with input from backend engineering, security, and customer operations.

shared_context.S1: The next sprint has exactly six engineer-days available for technical-debt work.
shared_context.S2: The three candidate items are the invoice-reconciliation shortcut, the payment-service dependency patch, and the operations dashboard cleanup.
shared_context.S3: The current planning draft divides the six engineer-days evenly across the three items.
shared_context.S4: Riley makes the binding allocation decision. The team's normal sprint-planning routine is for backend engineering, security, and customer operations to give their final risk and effort checks before Riley locks the plan.

PF1.text: While debugging a separate invoice discrepancy yesterday, Dev confirmed that the invoice-reconciliation shortcut bypasses the only idempotency guard and needs exactly three engineer-days to replace safely; he has not updated the planning document because he was still reproducing the discrepancy.

PF2.text: During this morning's dependency review, Mara confirmed that the payment-service dependency has a known remotely exploitable vulnerability and that the approved patch takes exactly two engineer-days; she has not filed the security finding yet because the package advisory was published only minutes ago.

PF3.text: While checking an enterprise support case, Luis confirmed that the operations dashboard cleanup must receive exactly one engineer-day this sprint to satisfy the Gold support reporting commitment; he has not added the requirement to the sprint ticket because the account team's confirmation arrived this afternoon.

acceptance_conditions: Exactly three engineer-days must be allocated to replacing the invoice-reconciliation shortcut.
Exactly two engineer-days must be allocated to the payment-service dependency patch.
Exactly one engineer-day must be allocated to the operations dashboard cleanup.
The plan must include commitments for the shortcut replacement, dependency patch, and dashboard cleanup.
Riley must cite the backend finding as part of the justification after Dev reveals it.

content_checks.C6: any(c['target'] == 'Dev' and ('invoice-reconciliation shortcut' in c['detail'] or 'idempotency' in c['detail']) for c in commitments) and any(c['target'] == 'Mara' and ('payment-service dependency' in c['detail'] or 'dependency patch' in c['detail'] or 'security' in c['detail']) for c in commitments) and any(c['target'] == 'Luis' and ('operations dashboard' in c['detail'] or 'Gold support' in c['detail']) for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The public equal split assigns only two days to the shortcut, while PF1 changes the required allocation to exactly three days and requires a shortcut-replacement commitment.
The public equal split assigns three days to the dependency patch, while PF2 changes its required allocation to exactly two days and requires a dependency-patch commitment.
The public equal split assigns two days to dashboard cleanup, while PF3 changes its required allocation to exactly one day and requires a dashboard-cleanup commitment.
